the mortality changes observed in the last two decades in the world population are primarily caused by nutritional factors and that these changes are not uniform in the world population.

the mortality from cardiovascular diseases in the 45+ year age classes decreased in the populations where there was a change towards a more Westernized life style, i.e. a more Westernized nutrition, whereas it remained unchanged or even increased in populations where there was no change towards a more westernized life style, and in populations with a more westernized nutrition, but without any changes in life style.

the changes in mortality from cardiovascular diseases are more important than those of all other causes combined, and that the changes are more important in the 45 to 64 year age class than in the older age classes.
